Start with a loss matrix: expected fraud loss, false-decline cost, review cost, and customer friction. At 0.02% prevalence, raw accuracy is useless; evaluate precision/recall and expected loss at the operational review/decline thresholds, then calibrate probabilities on representative prevalence.

A sub-50ms path should use precomputed velocity counters, device/account aggregates, and cached graph-risk features. Fetch them with parallel bounded calls, not an unbounded graph traversal at authorization time. Deduplicate payment events and distinguish event time from ingestion time. A fallback policy for missing features should be explicitly risk-tiered, not universally approve or decline.

Train on chargebacks and confirmed reviews with delay-aware labels. Review outcomes are selectively observed, so log selection and retain controlled audits where feasible. A review queue needs capacity-aware prioritization and SLA monitoring. Track fraud tactics, feature drift, false declines by cohort, and model calibration; use champion/challenger deployment and rapid rollback. Treat external features and identity signals as sensitive, access-controlled data.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For a simple approve/decline choice, decline when predicted expected fraud loss exceeds expected false-decline and intervention cost, using a validated cost model. At very low prevalence, precision depends heavily on false positives and calibration. Include review capacity as a constraint, and test delayed labels and missing-feature fallback behavior before deploying a threshold.
